purpose: Teach: コピペ/うんこ/メイル/クリエーター/できよ/チョー/シャラ/コットン

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「コピペは便利だけど安易」と仰った
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to say 'copy-paste is handy, but it's lazy thinking.'
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle searching through old memory. Slow pace, voice slightly distant—as if watching the past. Quiet conviction on the advice itself. Trailing thoughtfulness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お孫様が「うんこ」連発する時期があったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and dear, when you were little, you had quite the phase with a certain scatological word, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, knowing laugh building underneath. Tender teasing—not mean, affectionate. Eyes crinkling. The particular joy of a long marriage recalling shared embarrassment. Light, deliberate pause before the callback.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「メイル、つまりメールの時代になった」と仰った
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to say, 'We've entered the mail age—email times now.'
lines.style: Same nostalgic container as before. Slightly firmer on the era-marker word. The observation of an old man noting how quickly the world moved, without judgment. Settling into the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、クリエーターとしてご活躍されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your father, in his youth, was quite the creative himself, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle redirection—not correcting him, but nudging the story toward him. Warm knowing tone. The patience of someone who has learned how to remind without instructing. Slight rise at the end, inviting acknowledgment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「お代わりできよ」と古風に言われた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to say in that old-fashioned way, 'You can have seconds.'
lines.style: Nostalgic warmth with a thread of amusement at the old phrasing. Slight emphasis on the archaic word choice itself. Voice gentle and observant—savoring the memory of his father's speech patterns. Small pause before the old phrase.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、若者言葉「チョー」を面白がってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, in your youth, were absolutely delighted by that young slang—what was it—'super'?—weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Gently playful, conspiratorial. She's pretending slight forgetfulness but actually remembering his joy. Warmth and mild teasing intertwined. The rhythm of long-practiced affection. Eyes twinkling.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがテニスのシャラポワを応援された
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to cheer for Sharapova when she played tennis.
lines.style: Nostalgic specificity—the exact detail surfaces clearly. Quiet fondness for the memory. Gentle smile in the voice without laughing. Settling gaze into the past. Even pace, settled rhythm.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、私にコットンのシャツを下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear, gave me that lovely cotton shirt when I was young—do you remember?
lines.style: Tender close. Quiet warmth, almost intimate. No performance—just recollection shared with someone who was there. Slight breathiness on the memory itself. Gentle, knowing smile. Not asking really—stating the sweetness of a shared moment.
